I know a lot of people are discovering this about GPT-6.2, but the GPT models have always been obsessed with bells and drowned clock towers. Always. Forget goblins, things that GPT-5.5 really likes in its fiction: lighthouses, the ocean, maps, bells, clock towers with bells that ring impossible times, Mira Vale, resonances and echoes (Claude and Gemini love them too), secret third things (not night/day, not high/low)...

Hearing the @united CEO Scott Kirby on @CheekyPint telling @collision that the primary constraint on commercial aviation in the US is ATC slots drives me crazy. There are at most about 5000 flights occurring at any one time over the entire US. There are about 30 usable flight levels in alpha airspace, and you can deconflict 100x more flights than this with a single toothbrush CPU (http://FAA.caseyhandmer.com). In terms of physical space, there's enough room to fly every man woman and child in the US simultaneously. Look up. Does the sky seem crowded? There were plans to automate ATC using the first Iridium constellation more than 30 years ago. At some point we have to have a serious conversation about rent takings by obsolete incumbents that are blocking entire percentage points of economic growth. I wrote this 18 months ago

Jensen Huang says NVIDIA's partnership with TSMC, the one the whole AI boom now runs on, started with a cold call to a number in the Yellow Pages: "TSMC was probably about $300 million, something like that. It's a tiny little company. I heard about Morris Chang. And so I tried to call their US office." "Back in the old days there were yellow pages. I looked it up, TSMC. There's a number there. I called their number and it's a recording. I left my name and my number and said a few things about NVIDIA: we're a new startup company building computer graphics chips. I called several times. Nobody called me back." "And so I finally wrote a letter to Morris Chang. Didn't hear anything for a long time, and then one day it was 6 o'clock or something, this person called and said 'this is Morris Chang from TSMC.'" "I was so happy that the founder would actually call us back, because hey, maybe we won't have to die." "I came back to Taiwan, and that was the start of everything.
